levers.lever: Prepare one rule at a time inside a project cohort: declare every root to the shared walk as now, but evaluate a root's non-walk inputs in that rule's own delivery, right before its invocation, so they are released before the next rule's inputs are built. Shared producers keep their reader counts and are released after their last reader. Scheduling only: same regions, same delivery order, byte-identical findings, no new data structure.
levers.size: execution_runtime facade_runtime/project_execution.rs evaluate_roots and runtime/service/scheduling prepare_roots, about 150-300 lines plus project_phase tests
levers.evidence: h5, h9: 2169 MB of capture rows built in the first delivery's prepare_roots
levers.expected: the project phase is the largest single rule's inputs plus 1.56 GB of residual; unproven until measured

levers.lever: Let a row-local pure consumer continue on a capture's rows when the producer has several readers or the consumer keeps columns: a fan-out continuation, each reader getting the same rows in the same order, and a reshaping Select/Project writing into its scratch row, so the capture's output is never published whole. Changes fusion classification and the region continuation, not representations.
levers.size: execution_domain executable_program/fusion/service.rs (shape, fusibility_of), the region compiler and the kernel session continuation, about 600-1000 lines; larger
levers.evidence: h8; local-dependencies 3480084 rows, from paths 727134 rows, from 118446 source-dependency rows
levers.expected: removes most of the 2169 MB; also lowers file-phase materializations of the same shape
